Sorry this is late. Busy week at the @FRC household!

My last session was pretty productive. After last session, we cleaned all of the pine needles and sap from us, and took the corpses of the needleblights to a clearing and destroyed them to prevent their curse from spreading. Though, the druid knew enough about the beasts to tell us that there is probably Gulthias tree somewhere in the area. We didn't have time to scour the woods, though, as our second mission was to head to a nearby farm where a man has locked himself in his barn for days.

After the group (Halfling paladin and human ranger, with the NPC dwarf cleric) arrive, we do indeed find "Old Sanders" locked away screaming about purple wyrms eating his livestock. Truth be told, we missed the fact the livestock were missing, and after searching the corn fields we narrowly avoided a surprise attack from three ankhegs. We handily defeat the beasts, and the deepingdale residents nearby throw a little party for us militiamen and donate what livestock and food they can to Old Sanders.

On our way back to Highmoon to report back in to with the Deepingdale militia we followed the Glaemril river. At the end of our first day of travel, we met a trade caravan heading out from Highmoon. After a good evening of chat and Dwarven ale, watch was started. A noise was heard, but not investigated, on the 1st watch. On the 3rd watch I have the previous watch join me to scout the area. With a little help from detect magic, we barely spotted a goblin ambush on the camp!

Having had most of the night to prepare, 2 goblin groups were able to flank the camp. The cleric and myself (Halfling paladin) were able to hold back the main group long enough to break their morale and have them retreat, while the caravan guards were able to hold off the flankers until we could assist.

I was glad we were able to get so much done this session, as we usually run out of time and can only complete one encounter. This should just about close off our pre-campaign play, where the players got to learn the style of 5e (we're both experienced tabletop players, but new to 5e while the DM has been playing through the playtest) and set up some more backstory of how we got to know each other.

Our group embarked on a 50 day caravan, pretending to be guards. I won't go into too much detail as to avoid HotDQ spoilers but here is a picture of our DMs setup with the overhead projector :) http://i.imgur.com/oIgNP1G.jpg

It is fairly complicated but I made a post about it earlier: link. If you have some virtual map images to use then you could do a more simplistic "static" setup by just mounting the projector facing down and throwing the image on the table.
